text:
sara_sales: Hey @mike_se — customer (ACME) wants a Private deployment POC. They prefer PrivateLink but asked what we actually need from their side: subnets, route tables, DNS, SGs, and whether VPC peering is an option. Quick guidance?

mike_se: PrivateLink is the easiest for cross-account POCs. We expose an endpoint service; the consumer creates an interface VPC endpoint. Ask them for 2 private subnets (one per AZ) with at least /28 free IPs and a security group that allows outbound HTTPS to our service. Private DNS (enablePrivateDns) will map our service name to endpoint ENI IPs in their VPC.

julia_netops: Notes for their network team: interface endpoints don't require route table changes (that’s for gateway endpoints). Important items:
- pick subnets in 2 AZs
- ensure NACLs allow ephemeral ports (1024-65535) for ENI responses
- ensure SG allows outbound 443 and inbound from the endpoint SG if they lock down SGs

Sample consumer CLI to create endpoint (replace ids):
```bash
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \n  --vpc-id vpc-0123456789abcdef0 \n  --service-name com.amazonaws.vpce.us-east-1.vpce-svc-0abc1234 \n  --vpc-endpoint-type Interface \n  --subnet-ids subnet-aaa111 subnet-bbb222 \n  --security-group-ids sg-0a1b2c3d \n  --private-dns-enabled
```

julia_netops: Also: if they use private DNS, make sure they don't have a conflicting private hosted zone for the same name. Otherwise we can provide the ENI IPs or a dedicated hostname to use.

infra_ops: On our side we'll need the consumer AWS account ID to whitelist in the endpoint service permissions. We'll provide the service id (vpce-svc-0abc1234) and the account. Command we run to grant access: 
```bash
aws ec2 modify-vpc-endpoint-service-permissions \n  --service-id vpce-svc-0abc1234 \n  --add-allowed-principals arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root
```
We'll also share the full service-name string and owner account ID in DM.

security_eng: TLS + auth: we terminate TLS at our ALB and use standard public certs. For POCs we use token-based API keys with short TTLs. If they require mTLS or client cert auth we can enable it but that adds config. Also log flow: recommend they enable VPC flow logs during the POC for troubleshooting. We keep audit logs on our side.

sara_sales: Bonus Q — they asked about API key rotation and Dedicated pool access. For the POC we'll create scoped API keys that expire in 7 days. If they want Dedicated, that typically requires a reserved pool and network setup — can be via PrivateLink or dedicated network attachment; we'll scope that after POC.

mike_se: For testing once endpoint is up, they can curl our private hostname with the test key: 
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_test_abc123" https://private.redwood.example.com/v1/health
```
(If private DNS enabled, the name resolves to endpoint ENIs.)

deploy_bot: notice: create-vpce-service requested in redwood-infra-us-east-1. svc-id=vpce-svc-0abc1234 owner=arn:aws:iam::098765432109:root

julia_netops: Extra checklist we usually send to customers for PrivateLink POC: 
- provide consumer account ID
- provide two subnet IDs (one per AZ) and their CIDRs
- confirm security group rules (allow outbound 443)
- confirm NACLs allow ephemeral ports
- decide if private DNS is ok or they prefer IPs
- enable VPC flow logs for troubleshooting

sara_sales: Perfect — can you drop the service-name, owner account, and that checklist as a short message I can forward to their network team? Need it by EOD.

mike_se: Will DM service-name, owner account, and a one-page checklist now. I'll also include the CLI snippet and the sample curl.

sara_sales: Thanks all, sending to customer now. I’ll follow up here if they hit any blockers.
